items.caption:
day one.

i packed light. mostly questions.
the sky did not ask who i used to be —
it just made room.

30 days. 30 pages. i'm writing them in the sky.
if you're starting something too — a semester, a city,
a version of yourself — walk with me.

field notes, page one.

the room hums. no talking this afternoon — just observing.
i used to think watching from the edge meant i didn't belong.
now i think it means i'm paying attention.

everything i notice becomes material.
everything i keep becomes me.

what did you notice today that nobody else did?

night pages, 22:00.

learning the difference between alone and lonely.
the room hums. the page glows.
tonight is just quiet — and quiet is enough.

alone is a room you choose. lonely is a room that chooses you.
i'm practicing choosing. some nights i'm better at it than others.
if tonight is one of the other nights for you, you're not the only one awake.

items.caption:
it has been over a month now.
things have begun to roll and unfold
the way they do every fall.

ridiculously hot for october.
but the familiar smell of change
has started to settle over these aged grounds.

i think back to the summer
and realize how beautiful memories are.
and how experiences are nothing
without storage.

so i'm storing them. all of them.
that's what this page is.

i miss last year.
march. parties. summer.
saturday night.
ten minutes ago.

time is two faced.
time is strength.
time is the answer.

it begins tonight. i begin tonight,
in my dreams. my thoughts die
and relive tonight.

when my eyes reopen in the morning
i will be new. different.
i will be a change.

i have decided to change my life.

this is day one.

i spill it all out on the table
like an unwritten script,
a blank blueprint,
a radical idea.

no distractions. just the creation of ideas,
the reflection of ideas,
and above all, the search for answers.

NO. the creation of answers.

i'm not here to say i'm taking
some spiritual journey to find "who i am."

i'm here to make answers.
to make myself.

i don't know exactly what i'm looking for.
who does?
but i know my duty is to look.

i cannot describe this idea to anyone
except me.
and now, i guess, to you.

i bow my head to the past,
but the future kneels to me.

i wrote that at 18 in a notebook
nobody was ever supposed to read.

i still believe it.
some nights it's the only thing i believe.
that's enough to sleep on.

her laugh was the first thing i noticed.
i couldn't get enough of it,
and honestly i was jealous to hear it
knowing i wasn't part of it.

we clicked easily. then time and people
grew us apart. i stepped down
and turned away to hide what i felt.
the last thing i wanted
was to make it harder on you.

i got to know her in fragments.
maybe that's all we ever get of anyone.

i'm learning to love the fragments.

we talked every day for a while.

the way you talk to someone
when you don't know yet
what you are to each other.

there was a morning she asked me something
and i answered and then she laughed
and i thought: right. this.
i thought it clearly.
then i let it go.

i'm not sure why i keep doing that.
letting clear things go.

i had a dream of a girl.
i told her that her name
reminded me of a musical instrument
and she smiled back at me
with such radiance.

i woke up and wrote it down
before it could leave.

some people visit you in dreams
just to remind you
that your heart still works.

it does. it's working right now.

3:30pm. i just finished developing
a new roll of film
and i nearly quarantined the whole art building
with one spilled tray.

there was a woman at training yesterday.
eyes on success. degree, job, direction, done.
she actually enjoyed it. and i sat there thinking
where's the mystery? where is the excitement?

i could never live so basic.

i don't say that to be better than anyone.
i say it because i checked,
and there's something else in me.

the thing about mystery
is it's rarely somewhere else.
it's the same room
at a different angle.

that spilled tray this morning
made a shape i won't see again.
i stood there looking at it
longer than i needed to.

that's all mystery asks, i think.
just: stop. look.

you don't have to go anywhere.

items.caption:
developing film is controlled waiting.

you already took the picture.
the moment already happened.
now you stand in the red dark
and find out what you actually saw.

i think feelings work like this too.
some of mine are still in the chemicals.

i'll know what they were
when they're ready to surface.
i can wait.

i gave a dollar to a stranger this morning.

why did i reach into my pocket?
by the look of things that dollar wasn't
going anywhere good. that thought hurt.
but i don't regret it. it felt like a duty.

she put herself on the line to ask.
maybe that effort earned it.

a dollar is small.
deciding what kind of person you are
is not.

the thing about living in a city
is you're surrounded
and alone in the same moment.

i sat in the window for a while today
watching people walk by.
nobody saw me.
i wasn't bothered.

i was the window.
just watching the light move through.

there's a version of lonely
that isn't sad.
it's just: quiet.

i'm getting better at that one.

for the first time in a while, i feel lonely.

i feel alone and wistful.
and yet, somehow, it feels amazing.

not because being alone is the goal.
because this quiet is mine. chosen.
a room, my art, my notebooks,
a door i can open whenever i want.

i know i'm doing the right thing.
the proof is that i can sit here
with just myself
and still want tomorrow.

items.caption:
he asked me, "where do you want to go man?
anywhere you want!"

i had no voice. i struggled
to push out the words:

"i'm just happy."

that night on the bench means everything.
some places are the birth of who you are.
mine is a bench on a road at night
with my brother laughing in the cold.

find your bench. write it down.
you'll need the proof later.

there was a girl.

or there wasn't, exactly.
there was the feeling of a girl — which is different.
the want was real.
i remember the specific morning when i understood it.

but there was this other thing.
a thing i was in the middle of.
something i was trying to become.

and i knew if i chose the feeling,
i would lose the thread of the thing.

so i put it down.
the whole idea of it.
that's the hardest kind of down to put.
i've never told anyone that.

one week.
i wrote almost every day.

that's the first time in a long time
i did the thing i said i would do.

i keep waiting for it to feel like more.
it just feels like:
i wrote.
i showed up.

maybe that's the more.
maybe i've been measuring wrong.

i know what i want.
that's the honest part.
i've known it for a while.

the question is always:
now or after?

and i keep choosing after.

i'm not sure what i'm waiting for.
i think i'm waiting
until it costs less.

it never costs less.
i keep thinking it will.

day seven. one week of pages.

what i know so far:
memories are beautiful. storage is everything.
laughter you're not part of can still teach you.
film develops in darkness and so do i.
a dollar can be a duty.
lonely and alone are not the same word.

what i don't know yet
could fill the rest of this notebook.

good. that's what the notebook is for.

see you tomorrow.

i got choked up watching them.

not because i wanted what they had.
or — not only that.

it was recognition.
the specific feeling of: i know what that is.
i know exactly why i don't have it right now.

i chose this.
the question over the answer.
the quest over the arrival.

that's the thing about chosen costs —
you chose them.
that doesn't make them free.

i make diagrams when the words run out.

boxes. arrows. labels.
the elements of confusion, i called this one.
each box is a thing i don't understand.

there were a lot of boxes.

i drew lines between some of them —
not because i planned to,
but because when you look at the boxes long enough
you start seeing how they talk to each other.

that was the first time i thought:
maybe not knowing has a structure.
i've been trying to read it ever since.

i make diagrams when the words run out.
twenty-two boxes this time.
none of them connected.

i kept drawing anyway.

there's something useful in that.
not the diagram.
the drawing.
the act of trying to trace
something you don't understand yet.

the tracing is the thing.

someone gestured at the sky once and said: all of that.

i nodded.

but i wasn't looking out.
i was thinking about the courtyard.
the smell of the air in october.
the particular sound of a room at 11pm.

the infinite is fine.
i use it as a dismissal.
there's more going on in here.

i've been thinking about what perfect would look like.

not the title.
not the announcement.

just:
waking up and it's you.
still here. still easy.
no performance required.

the closeness.
not the category.
that's what i keep coming back to.

i think i always knew what i was looking for.
i just didn't have a word for it that fit.

i keep imagining it wrong.
like it has to be grand.

but when i'm honest
it's smaller than that.

it's just:
still here.
still easy.
coffee somewhere.
not performing.

that's the whole thing.
i've been dramatizing what is actually just
wanting someone to stay.

the hardest thing i ever did
was turn away from something i wanted
to finish something i needed.

not because i didn't want it.
because i owed myself something first.

a version of me that wasn't held together
by someone else's gravity.

i've never fully explained that to anyone.
but i think about it
more than i let on.

there's a thing that happens
when someone gets close enough.

my heart starts acting like it wants out.
not from them —
from me. from the walls i built around it.

it doesn't ask permission.
it just starts pressing.

i don't always know what to do with that.
but i've stopped pretending it doesn't happen.

it's happening right now,
writing this.

the thing i don't say often:
i want to let people in.

i built the walls.
i know exactly where they are.
but i still want to be found in them.

that's not a contradiction.
that's just being human and scared
and still wanting
anyway.

the crack in the wall isn't damage.
it's the door.

some feelings have timers on them.

they don't detonate dramatically.
they just go off at 2pm on a tuesday
while you're thinking about something else.

and then you know.
you've been carrying it for a while.
the timer ran out quietly.

you're the last one to find out.

i woke up disgusted with myself.

not at anyone else.
not at the situation.
at the parts of me i'd been feeding
that didn't deserve to be fed.

that feeling —
that sick, clear, morning feeling —
was the most useful thing i'd felt in months.

i started keeping a different kind of list after that.
not goals. not plans.
just: what do i actually want to be?

i love myself more
when i'm honest about that question.

by afternoon
the sick feeling was just
information.

i wrote down what i didn't like.
not to complain.
to change it.

there's a real difference.
complaining points at the thing.
changing walks toward it.

i'm trying to learn
the difference between pointing
and moving.

some nights the world is
just surface.

everybody performing their version
of a good time.
and i'm standing there thinking:
this is barely it.
this is barely human.

i don't say that to be separate.
i say it because i wanted more.
meat on the bone. depth. real asking.

so i went quiet.
i waited.
i'm still waiting, a little.
but i know what i'm waiting for now.

someone close to me noted once —
casually, mid-conversation —
that most of what came out of people's mouths
was negative.

ninety percent, roughly.
complaint. comparison. competition.

i sat with that for a long time.
not because it made me angry.
because when i actually listened —
to rooms, to tables, to myself —
i couldn't argue.

noticing a pattern is not the same as breaking it.
but you can't break what you haven't found.

i tried it today.
somebody walked by
and i just said:
that's a good color on you.

they stopped.
genuinely surprised.
and then they smiled.

it cost me nothing.
i mean nothing.
i don't know why i don't do this more.

the 10%
doesn't ask much.
just: try something different.

i had a dream.

i was on a battlefield.
not a movie one.
a real one, somehow, with real weight.

and i just stopped.
i dropped what i was carrying.
i turned and ran.

the dream kept going but my body
was already deciding:
this isn't the war i signed up for.

i woke up clear.
that clarity lasted a few days.
i'm trying to keep some of it.

there's this kind of grief
that doesn't have a reason.

we didn't fight.
nobody did anything wrong.
we just — stopped.

i miss talking to them.
the ease of it. the way it felt
like i could say the half-finished thought
and they'd finish it.

that doesn't happen often.
when it's gone and you don't know why
you don't get to be angry.
you just miss it.

i went to text you today.
opened the thread.
scrolled up a while.

there we are.
talking about nothing.
like there was all the time.

i closed it.
i don't know what to say yet.

i'll think of something eventually.
or i won't.
that's the grief part —
you don't get to know
which one it'll be.

two weeks of pages.

what i've learned:
the quest costs real things.
the hardest down to put is the one you chose.
not knowing has a structure.
infinity is background — this is foreground.
a friendship can end without a villain.

what i still don't know:
when to stop choosing the question
and let someone else be the answer.

good.
that's what the next two weeks are for.

she said it once.
in passing. mid-conversation.
like she was talking about the weather.

"you're more than you're being right now."

i didn't know what to do with that.
so i argued.
in my head. later. for weeks.

kept losing.

everything i was running from
was also running away from me —
that's the thing i figured out
at 3am when i finally stopped running.

the chains were mine.
i was the one holding them.

coming back wasn't surrender.
it was the first thing i decided on purpose.

somebody told me
i was built for something bigger.
not her — someone else.
but i thought of her when i heard it.

weird how a person can live in a sentence
they didn't say.

i argued with both of them.
in my head. at home.
the one who said it.
and the one who didn't.

i kept losing.

at some point you stop arguing
and you just try it on.
see what it does to the way you walk.

there was a night i stopped performing.

not dramatically. not on purpose.
i just ran out of material.

and what was left —
the thing underneath the thing —
was louder than anything i'd been saying.

she wasn't there to hear it.
neither was anyone.

but i heard it.
and i know what it is now.
and i know it's mine.
and i know it's not nothing.
that part doesn't need an audience.

nobody in my family
had walked through this door before.

i didn't know that going in.
or i knew it and didn't feel it yet.

my brother came to visit once
and we stood outside
looking up at the building.

he didn't say anything.
i didn't say anything.

then he said: "what's it like inside?"

and i said: "different."

and he nodded like he already knew.
that was the whole conversation.
i've been writing it down ever since.

i didn't know what would be on the other side.
i just knew
nobody in my family had come this way before.

and that felt like:
either a warning
or a permission slip.

i took it as a permission slip.
that's probably the only thing
that made the difference.

somebody has to go first.
i don't know why it was me.
but i'm writing the directions
for whoever comes after.
they won't need to be afraid of the door.

i used to read the difference
as something to explain.

as if being the first meant
i owed the room a translation.

but there was a night
i stopped translating.

and what came out
was something i hadn't said before.
unfiltered. unmapped.
mine on purpose.

the room was quiet.
then somebody laughed —
not at it.
with something they recognized.

the difference isn't the obstacle.
the difference is the whole thing.

somebody i admired said:

stop trying to write your way out.
read the room you're in.

i spent a year
trying to write my way out of everything.

then i stopped.
and read the room.

the cage is the story.
the bars are where it gets interesting.
the resolution is not the point.

finding the bars —
that's the whole education.

i've been reading the bars.

some of them are real.
some of them are stories
i've been telling long enough
that they calcified.

there's a difference between a wall
and a word that behaves like a wall.

the word kind is easier to work with.
all you need is a different word.

i've been finding different words.
it's slow work.
but it's mine.
i can feel where each one loosens.

here's what nobody tells you:

you can't dismantle what you haven't named.

i spent a year just naming things.
this is fear.
this is inheritance.
this is a story i borrowed
from someone who borrowed it from someone else.

most of it i'm returning.
but some of it was useful.
and now it's mine on purpose.

not a cage.
a frame.

you build different things
when you know the difference.

there's a version of my life
that would have been fine.

and i mean fine.
not as an insult.
genuinely — stable, soft-edged, no complaint.

she was in that version.
or someone like her.
i know that now.

but i had this question in me
that would not sit down.

and every time i got close to fine
the question stood up.

so i followed the question.
that's the whole story.
so far.

i think about fine sometimes.

fine would have been easier.
i'm not going to pretend otherwise.

but every time i get close to it
there's this thing that says:

is this it?

and the answer keeps coming back:
not yet.
not yet.
not yet.

and so i keep walking.
and the question keeps walking with me.
that's okay.
i've started to like the company.

i used to apologize for how hard it was.

as if difficulty were a design flaw.
as if struggle meant i chose wrong.

but i've stopped apologizing.

because the things that came easy
slid right off.
and the things that cost something —

a relationship i didn't start.
a city i chose alone.
a version of myself
that hadn't proven anything yet —

those became part of the structure.

i want a life with texture in it.
i want to run my hand across it
and feel where i was.

there is a specific feeling
that comes late at night
when the building empties
and i'm still working.

not loneliness.
something closer to: finally.

i start moving differently.
thinking differently.

she used to ask me what i was working on so late.
i never had a good answer.
i think the answer was: this.
exactly this.

the most honest version of what i'm doing
only shows up when nobody's watching.
except now i'm watching myself.
and writing it down while it happens.

the interesting thing
is it doesn't change
when people can see it.

i thought it would.
i thought the honest version
only lived at 2am
when nobody was watching.

but it's just there.
noon or midnight.
doing the thing.
not performing.

she once said: you only trust yourself
when you think no one's watching.

she was right.
i'm working on it.

some work only gets done at night.

not because of discipline.
because the day is full of
other people's urgency.

and at 1am the urgency runs out
and what's left is just:
what actually matters to you?

i find out what i actually believe
after midnight.
the rest is performance.

i'm learning to trust the night version.
i'm learning to bring it with me
into the day.

it's slower. more specific.
but it's mine.
both sides finally just dance.

somewhere in the middle of all this
i stopped treating want and work
like they were fighting.

they were both just trying
to get somewhere.

i think of her sometimes.
the way that want felt.
specific. warm. real.

and i think: yeah.
that was never the enemy.

i was standing at the wrong angle.
i was measuring the wrong distance.

the question and the answer
were always in the same room.
i was the one who kept leaving.

i used to think
wanting and working were opposites.

i don't remember where i got that.
some version of discipline
that punished softness.

she laughed easily.
work was hard for me to do lightly.

they were never in competition.
they're the same motion
in the same direction.

i wasted some time on the wrong idea.
but time spent learning to see
is not wasted.

experiences are nothing without storage.
i'm storing this one.

i've been here three weeks.

i can see what i came from
if i look back.
i can see what's ahead
if i look forward.

but right now i'm just trying to stay
in the middle of the arc.

there's a version of me
who got what he wanted.
there's a version who built what he needed.

i think they're both in here.
the air is different in the middle.
i don't want to rush through it
to get to whatever's next.

three weeks.

and the thing i keep noticing is:
i've stopped needing to know what comes next
in order to show up for today.

that's new for me.

the open road used to feel like a threat.
now it just feels like the road.

i wrote that at 3am.
i wasn't sure i meant it.
in the morning i read it back.
i still meant it.

that's the test.
see you on the other side of this.

three weeks ago
i would have planned the next seven things.

i do that less now.
not because i don't care.
because showing up for today
turned out to be enough
to get to tomorrow.

she used to plan everything.
i watched her and realized:
i had confused planning
with living.

they're not the same.
one gets you somewhere.
the other keeps you from being where you are.

small thing.
mine though.

three weeks of pages.

what i've learned:
you can return and still be moving forward.
being first means writing the directions.
the cage is the story, not the obstacle.
refusing the safe path isn't reckless.
some work only happens after midnight.
want and work go the same direction.

what i still don't know:
how to let someone in
without losing the thread of the thing.

good.
that's what the next two weeks are for.

it has been four months
since i tucked you away.

four months of turning
much of my mind off,
of waking, working, sleeping,
of calling that a life.

the drawer never complained.
that's the trick of drawers —
they keep what you give them
exactly as you left it,
the ink still wet somewhere
underneath the dust.

i've missed you.
i need you now more than ever.

some part of me knew
to write that like a promise.

this morning i'm keeping it.

it has been easier
to turn much of my mind off
and drag along this linear path.

easier is the word
that scares me now.

wake, class, work, sleep.
the path asks nothing.
it gives nothing.
it just keeps offering itself,
flat and endless and polite.

and the whole time
something in me stood
at the edge of the asphalt,
looking out at the grass,
holding a question
like a coat i refused
to put down.

i'd rather carry the question
than the quiet.

i'm off the line now.

i've missed you and i need you
now more than ever.

i wrote that to a notebook.
eighteen years old,
talking to paper
like it could answer.

and here is what i've learned
in all the years since:
it answers.
slowly, in your own handwriting,
years later, at midnight,
when you finally come back
and read what you were
brave enough to leave.

there is a thinking
that only happens when you write —
the sentence goes somewhere
you didn't plan,
and you find out what you meant.

if you have a version of this —
a notebook, a note app, a napkin —
open it tonight.
it's been waiting.

experience is age.

three words i wrote at eighteen
and didn't understand until now.

not birthdays. not years
stacked up like quiet plates.
experience —
the nights you actually felt,
the conversations you didn't perform,
the mornings you wrote
before the world could edit you.

by that math, some people
are older at nineteen
than others at fifty.
by that math, a single honest month
can age you like a decade
of weather.

this month made me ancient.

i mean that as a blessing.

"this is stupid."
"that's ridiculous."
"change the channel."

my father caught me saying
those three things while we
watched television together.
he pointed out they made up
ninety percent of my speech.

he wasn't wrong.
i had opened my spirit
to negative energy
and called it taste.
i had confused contempt
for standards,
complaint for vision.

the subconscious keeps the books
either way — every word
a deposit somewhere.

ninety percent is a lot
of speech to get back.

i started that night.
i'm still at it.

after submerging myself
in the friend gatherings,
i realized why i began this quest.

that's all the entry says.
it doesn't explain.
i remember anyway.

rooms full of people i liked
where i still went quiet.
laughter i loved from a distance
i couldn't seem to close.
whole evenings spent
watching the warmth
like weather through glass.

the quest was never
to escape those rooms.
it was to be able to stand in them
as someone i had made on purpose —
to walk in carrying a self
i could actually offer.

i'm closer now.
pages closer.

items.caption:
to many, the word infinity
is a comfortable dismissal
of the unknown.

i wrote that in a letter
i never sent.

people say infinity
the way they say whatever —
a word for the door
they've decided not to open.

but look beyond
the scenery of it all.
our social existence
is confined by definition.
our primordial is not.

i didn't know what primordial
meant at eighteen.
i just knew there was a bigger room,
and that the walls i kept touching
were furniture, not architecture.

i'm still walking toward it.
i hope i never arrive.

i lay interest upon
the yard beyond the door
and the road beyond the yard.

eighteen, restless
for no reason except my own head,
i mapped the world in layers:
door. yard. road. horizon.
each one a skin
the next one waited under.

let go of what you think you need,
what you think you want,
what you think will make you happy —
i wrote that too, the same winter.
it's not finding yourself.
it's making yourself.

i've since learned
every layer is a door.
you never run out.

that used to scare me.
now it's the best news i have:
the yard keeps going.
the road keeps starting.

at this very exact moment,
i have no idea what i want.

i drew a diagram under that sentence.
the elements of confusion —
arrows everywhere, circles,
no legend, no north.

and then one line at the bottom,
like a flare in the dark:

everything makes sense in between.

not before. not after. in between.
darkness was definitely not a mistake —
i wrote that the same night.

confusion isn't the absence
of the map.
it is the map, mid-draw,
the hand still moving,
the ink still deciding.

i'm still drawing.
that's the sense it makes.

i long for the contact of another —
but instead of simple pleasures
i would rather a mutual understanding,
a collaborative existence.

someone who understands the magic
of being together
for the sake of being together.

no occasion. no performance.
two people in the same afternoon,
letting it be enough.

happiness comes from
the infinite extension of the self —
i believed that alone
in a dorm room,
and i believe it more now,
because the self extends furthest
in the presence of another
who is also reaching.

eighteen-year-olds
aren't supposed to write that.
i did.

i still mean every word.

quoting my father:
"you will never find
a girl like that."

he meant it kindly.
that's the hardest way to mean it —
love, dressed as arithmetic,
trying to save me
from my own wanting.

i wrote his sentence down
so i could keep disagreeing with it
in writing.

maybe he's right.
maybe the person i described
doesn't exist.

but i wasn't describing a person.
i was describing a standard.

and standards don't have to exist yet.
that's what makes them standards.
that's what makes them mine.

i realized i was dying
when it is your heart
escapes you within the reckless
and regretfully irrational
grip of another.

that's verbatim —
the grammar breaking
under the weight of the feeling,
and i refuse to fix it.

the ticking time bomb,
its hour and minute hand
as the inhale and exhale
of devotion.

it really does suck.
that's verbatim too.

but here is what eighteen
couldn't see yet:
caring about someone
means handing them the clock.

and i'd rather hand someone the clock
than never learn to tell time.

items.caption:
in the game of infinite play,
my decision to begin my change
was only a continuation
of participation.

i am now free to play infinitely
and not have to synthesize boundaries.

translation, from eighteen to now:
there is no finish line.
there never was one.
the game doesn't end —
it deepens.

finite players play to win,
and winning ends the game.
infinite players play
to keep playing,
and the field keeps growing
to meet them.

somewhere in that first cold spring,
i chose.

i'd choose it again this morning.
i choose it every morning.

i am an artist
and difference is a natural.

five words of grammar trouble
and i still can't say it better.

difference is a natural.
not a burden you explain at parties.
not a gap you apologize across.
a natural — like weather,
like left-handedness,
like the particular slant of light
you were born under.

the first of my family to walk
through that particular door,
and the difference walked in with me,
sat down at the easel,
and asked what we were making.

it's the material.
it always was.

everything i've ever made
is made of it.

i'm pretty content.
my room is pretty rad
with all of the art hung up.
plenty of memories to cherish.
i'm stable and i have returned.

no metaphor tonight.
just a kid in a room he made,
surrounded by things he made,
calling it rad
in his own handwriting.

after all the war journals,
the transformations,
the declarations at midnight —
five plain sentences
about a room.

some entries you outgrow.
some you grow into.

this one i'm still growing into:
the discipline of being
simply, unspectacularly
okay.

items.caption:
finally gathering up enough courage
to at least begin
pushing for something.

that's how i wrote it —
at least begin.
courage measured in teaspoons.

nobody tells you that's allowed.
that you can be brave in installments.
that the hand can hover at the door
for a whole season
and the knock still counts.

there had been eons of change
since july — his words,
hungover at work, killing time,
still proud of the teaspoon.

the door doesn't care
whether you knocked confidently.
it just cares that you knocked.

so knock.

i cannot comfortably say
that it's unfolding nicely.
but something is happening.

i want to frame that sentence.

not it worked out.
not it fell apart.
something is happening —
the honest middle
of every true thing,
where the leaves are still in the air
and nobody knows yet
where they land.

i know our friendship is too strong
for something like this to destroy it.

i wrote that to convince myself.
it turned out to be true anyway —
which is its own kind of miracle:
the sentences we tell ourselves
to keep walking,
that quietly come true.

i can't keep holding back so much.
i want to live a little bit.

i built a monk's life at eighteen —
no distractions, no tv, no girls.
the creation of ideas.
the reflection of ideas.
above all, the search for answers.
NO — the creation of answers.

and then one november night,
tired and honest,
i wrote the other sentence:
i want to live a little bit.

the discipline wasn't wrong.
it built the room —
every wall, every shelf,
every quiet hour of it.

but a room is for living in.

both sentences were me.
both were right.

it took years to let them
shake hands.

as i read my first entry last night,
i could still feel the intensity.

two and a half years after page one,
i went back and read myself.

i was young, naive, airy, hopeful.

i wrote that like an apology.
i read it now like a resume.

young enough to declare
a transformation out loud.
naive enough to believe it.
airy enough to float
over every reasonable doubt.
hopeful enough to write it down
where the future could find it.

page one knew things
the later pages forgot —
mostly that beginning at all
is the bravest sentence
anyone ever writes.

i'm not sure what happened
but so much has changed.

no dramatic scene.
no turning point you could film.
just pages, stacking.

change doesn't announce itself.
it compounds —
quiet as interest,
patient as weather.
you look up from the notebook
one ordinary day
and the handwriting is the same
but the hand is not.

i find it frustratingly difficult,
i wrote, and i won't pretend
i didn't.
frustrating is the tuition.

still true.
still worth it.
still going.

four weeks of pages.

week one i declared a war
on my old self.
week two i chose the quiet
on purpose.
week three i resisted
everything warm,
just to prove i could.
week four i went back
for the notebook.

as i read it now,
i can still feel the intensity.
that's the part nobody promised —
that it keeps.
that a page holds heat
like a stone holds the sun,
years after the day
that warmed it.

two pages left.
i'm writing slower.

i want to mean every word.

dear fellow art comrade
and, above all, a great friend —

you are one of the few people
i can converse with about
life, beliefs, nature, and art.
you have a hungry spirit,
and that's what drew me
out of my tower —
the first human relationship
i explored on purpose
instead of by accident.

i truly appreciate your presence.
thanks for keeping me open.

THIS IS INFINITY.

i wrote that in a yearbook, basically.
all caps in the original.

some people don't change your life.
they change your appetite for it.

i stand by the caps.

my natural inclination is loneliness —
but read the whole sentence:

my natural inclination is loneliness.
artists provide me with reference
and cathartic lines of inspiration.
i work best at night.

it's not a confession.
it's a schedule.

the world hands you daylight,
small talk, fluorescent rooms.
you hand it back canvases.

the night doesn't ask
how you're doing.
it just moves the moon
a little out of your way
and lets you work.

alone was never the problem.
alone is the studio.

i enjoy my mental image
of a man alone in a room
dancing with cartesian dualism.

body and mind,
arguing for four centuries
about which one of them is real —
and the kid just
dances with both.

this might be my favorite sentence
my younger self ever wrote.
no audience.
no music anyone else could hear.
philosophy turned
into choreography,
loneliness turned
into a partner.

if the inclination is loneliness,
this is what you build on top of it:
a room, a record,
a self that moves.

undefeated.

items.caption:
the cage is the story.
forget the resolution
and find the bars!

i wrote that in a margin at nineteen,
reading someone else's book,
not knowing i was writing
the assignment
for the rest of my life.

thirty days ago
i opened this journal
looking for a resolution —
an ending, a verdict,
a door marked exit.

day thirty, and here
is the actual find:
the bars. named, numbered, mapped.
where each one came from.
which ones bend.
which ones were never locked.

the resolution can take its time.
i have the blueprint now —
and a blueprint in the right hands
is already a kind of open.

my brother said to me:
"when you can find someone
knowing what you want to share —
then you are free."

and i said: i am, bro.

one bench. two kids
from the same nowhere,
deciding out loud, to each other,
who they were going to be.

he asked me,
"where do you want to go, man?
anywhere you want!"
and i had no voice.
i struggled to push out the words:
i'm just happy.

that bench means everything to me.
it was the birth of our identities
as brothers.

freedom isn't a solo project.
someone has to hear
the answer you made.

i was 18 when i wrote this journal.
36 when i finally listened.

thirty days ago i started
publishing the way back,
one day at a time —
the tucked-away notebook,
the linear path, the bars,
the bench, the dance.

here is the last verbatim.
the first thing he ever wrote me:

i bow my head to the past,
but the future kneels to me.

he was right. i checked.
it kneels.

the notebook is full.
i am not.

thank you for reading him with me.
write yours down —
badly, bravely, tonight.
someday, some ordinary evening
decades from now,
you'll come looking
for the way back.

make sure it's there.

items.caption:
3:30pm.
i just finished developing
a new roll of film.

in the dark, in the chemicals,
the day swims back up —
faces, weather, an ordinary thursday
becoming permanent.

you have to stand in a dark room
to get the picture back.
nobody tells you that
about remembering.

the negatives dry on a line
like small black flags
of a country
i'm still founding.

a woman in yesterday's training
had eyes that only looked forward —
degree, job, direction, done.

she seemed happy.
i couldn't tell if that
frightened me or comforted me.

people will do just about
anything for money.
but where's the mystery?
where is the excitement?

i don't think i'm built for basic.
i checked the manual.
the part where it says settle
is missing from my copy.

there's this girl
who thinks she's the shit,
and tonight she dragged me
out of my dorm
and across a state line.

she always picks me up
when i'm just out of the shower.
she knows she does it
on PURPOSE.

some people arrive in your life
like weather.
you don't schedule them.
you just get rained on
and call it a good night.

i revealed my greatest secret.

i knew i had to
in order to change,
to love who i am,
to find who i am.

a secret is heavy
the way a seed is heavy —
all that future
packed in the dark.

i put it down in the light.
i watched it become
just a true thing that happened.

and then i watched it
start to grow.

figure out what you're doing
before you try to figure out
what you're doing.

i wrote it twice on purpose.

the first one is the compass.
the second one is the map.
most people draw the map first
and wonder why
every road on it
leads somewhere they don't want.

north before roads.
aim before effort.
question before question.

i have moved out
of the previous stage
and need to reach the next.

no diploma for it.
no ceremony.
just the quiet click
of a door closing itself
behind you
because you finally stopped
holding it open.

the stairs don't announce
themselves either.
you notice you're climbing
by how the air changes.

tonight the air changed.

last night the lunchroom
was a place of fake friendships
and judgments.
then the room changed —
became a country club,
a pool, a job i never had.

dreams renovate like that.
no permits. no warning.
the same people wearing
different rooms.

i'm learning to read
the architecture instead
of the faces.

the rooms know things
the faces won't say.

in the dream they asked me
to take off the reflective vest.

funny what you wear
to be seen
that was never yours.

borrowed brightness.
a stranger's idea of visible.

i'm taking inventory today:
which of my bright things
are mine,
which are costume.

what's mine can stay.
the rest comes off
one strap at a time,
in the light, on purpose.

he called me out
and knew i was lying.

even asleep
i keep an honest witness
on payroll.

the dream doesn't punish.
it just holds up the receipt
and waits.

so tomorrow: one true sentence.
said out loud, to a real person,
in a real room.

that's the whole assignment.
the witness rests
when the daylight version of me
starts telling the truth first.

i'm listening to
'all you need is love'
while writing this.
the radio has jokes.

everyone around me is pairing off
like the semester depends on it.
i want it too —
more than i say out loud.

but i'm mid-build.
the wanting is proof
the heart works.

i'm letting mine finish
becoming something
worth handing to somebody.

it really seems like
i'm just staying still
as i watch everyone else
move on.

that's how it looks
from the road, anyway.

but trees don't commute.
everything a forest does,
it does standing still —
the reaching, the ringing,
the slow underground handshake
of roots finding water.

i need to grow inside.
so i'm standing here,
growing inside.

the road can keep the traffic.

i'm eating chewy candy
and literally biting my way
back to my past.

as a kid, everything
was instant pleasure —
a bowl of ice cream,
new cartoons, a saturday
with no hands on its clock.

some nights you visit.
you don't move back in.

the kid is still here anyway,
running the projector,
keeping the colors warm
for whoever i'm becoming next.

tonight we watched together.

this university is like a candle.

i keep turning the sentence over.

maybe: it gives light
by spending itself.
maybe: it stands in a draft
and holds the flame anyway.
maybe: everything bright here
is burning through something
to stay bright.

i'll take the third one.
i know what i'm spending.
i'm watching what it buys.

the flame is worth the wax —
but only if you choose
what you light.

PROUD TO BE MUCH TOO BIG.

too big for the template.
too big for the polite size
of wanting they hand you
at the door.

first of my family
through these gates —
i didn't come this far
to fold myself
into a smaller font.

let the room adjust.
let the doorframes learn.

much too big
was never the problem.
the containers were.

i've taken a break from my quest,
just to refresh my mind.

not surrender. intermission.

even the moon takes
a night off a month
and nobody calls it quitting.

i'd rather write or paint anyway —
the quiet work that fills
the well back up.

the quest isn't going anywhere.
it's keeping my seat warm.

house lights up.
i'll be back before act two.

i was going to pass him
without eye contact.
he blatantly asked me
what my name was.

blatantly. imagine.
the audacity of just — asking.

it cost him nothing.
it rearranged my whole walk.

i said my name.
it sounded new
in a stranger's morning.

somewhere on campus
someone is carrying it now,
casually, like change
in a pocket. i hope
it buys him something.

why did i have the nerve
to almost walk right by him?

that's the question
i can't put down.

he reminded me of someone.
that was the whole crime.
i saw a mirror coming
and crossed the street.

the things i dodge in others
are the things
i haven't made peace with
in me.

noted. logged.
next time the mirror says hello,
i'm saying it back.

almost walked by.
almost stayed in.
almost let the whole thing
stay a stranger.

almost is where
most of a life gets stored —
the unopened doors,
polite and shut.

but tonight i'm counting
the ones i did open.

small list. good list.
every item on it
started as an almost
that lost.

i knew i had no business
being here this week.
so i convinced my father
to pick me up.

asked. out loud. for help.

the phone weighed
four hundred pounds
and then it weighed nothing.

he said yes
like it was the easiest
math of his life.

some doors you walk through.
some doors drive
two hours to get you.

i told my father about my change.
he listened and knew.

for the first time
i felt as if my father
saw me as a man.

not because i proved anything.
because i spoke
and he didn't look away.

there is a door in every father
that only opens
when the kid stops performing
and starts telling.

i told. it opened.
we stood in it together
a while.

the fight to hold back tears
escaped into a victorious loss.

read that again. i did.
a loss can be victorious
if what breaks
is only the dam.

driving the nightly roads home,
windows down, everything lit
like the town knew.

these roads will forever hold
an indestructible structure
to my existence.

some nights build you
a load-bearing wall.
this was one.

i've learned
not to force an entry.

the page can smell a fake.
so can the self.

some mornings the words
circle the field twice
and land on their own.
some mornings they don't,
and the honest move
is to leave the gate open
and go live a day
worth writing down.

today i'm living one.
the page can wait.
it likes me better
when i arrive full.

the battle to destroy
the false being within
will be as much our lives
as dreaming, creating, learning.

we shook on it, basically.
two kids and a mountain
and a sentence too big
for either of us.

the false being isn't a monster.
it's a costume that learned
my measurements.

every honest page
takes it in an inch.
every made thing
hangs it further back
in the closet.

dreaming. creating. learning.
that's the whole war.

confidence is a measure
fabricated from social standards.
i don't consider myself
confident at all.
i'm goofy. 'weird.' i'm me.

i lived in my basement
for three of my four years
of school.

what i do consider myself
is someone who wants more.

remember the math:
a basement plus a want
is not a basement.

it's a launchpad
with the lights off,
counting quietly
backwards.

i only wish for a chance
for things to realign.

not rewind. realign.

planets don't apologize
their way back into orbit.
they just keep to their paths,
patient, shining,
until the geometry
comes around again.

so i'll keep to my path
and stay bright enough
to be found.

the sky runs on schedules
we don't get to see.
alignment is one of them.

i wish only to talk
of happiness, growth, or life.

that's the whole menu.

not the weather of gossip.
not the sport of complaint.
give me one hour
and a person who wants
to grow out loud —

what are you making.
what is making you.
what would you do
if the fear called in sick.

three questions.
i'm buying the coffee.

i am sorry.
i miss being a friend.

not having one — being one.
the verb of it.
showing up. remembering
the small things. carrying
half of someone's ordinary day.

i stepped back from people
to build myself,
and the building is real.
but a self is for handing
to other people.
that's what it's for.

so this week: one message.
one door. one name
i've been meaning to say.

being a friend is a muscle.
i'm going back to the gym.

items.caption:
i cut one more chain.

not all of them.
one.

that's how it actually goes —
no montage, no anthem,
just a tuesday
and a pair of quiet hands
and one less thing
with my name on its leash.

count them the honest way:
not how many are left.
how many are off.

one more. one more.
the arithmetic of getting free.

my brother said:
'you're not a man, you're a god.'

brothers talk like that.
they see you through
a telescope pointed
at who you're becoming
and report it back
like the news.

i'm not a god.
most days i'm barely
on time.

but somebody i trust
looked at me and saw
the biggest possible weather.

i'm keeping the forecast.
i'd like to prove him
slightly right.

thanks.

that's the whole page tonight.

some days hand you
one good thing —
a friend, a save, a door
held open at the exact
right second —

and the only honest poetry
is a receipt.

thanks.
signed, sealed,
sleeping on it.

the courtyard, in the dream,
had lights strung up —
some sort of summer magic.

running, tackling, tickling,
laughing. that kind of night.
the kind you don't plan
and can't repeat.

she gave me looks that couldn't
have meant anything other
than the magic i've missed.

i woke up smiling
like a fool with a secret.

let the day try
to top that. i'll wait.

have trust in me.

i finally said it out loud —
all of it, no punctuation,
straight from the chest.

it's a strange ask.
trust is a bridge
you can only build
from both ends at once.

so here's my end:
i'll keep being exactly
who i say i am,
plank by plank,
until the middle meets.

that's all anyone
can put on the table.
i put it there.

her head on my shoulder.
i could feel what seemed to be
her pulse, pulsating
through her whole body.

our hands met.
i woke up.

then i was in an attic, writing.
then something chased me.
then i yelled 'give pass!'
and launched a pillow
across the actual room.

my roommate just stared.

somewhere in there
is a whole philosophy.
tonight i'm just glad
the heart keeps drumming
even in the dream.

i felt back
for the first time
since december.

feeling comes back
the way spring does —
not all at once,
one warm edge at a time,
ice giving up the field
in small defeats.

december was long.
i kept the pilot light on.
that counts more
than anyone tells you.

this morning: thaw.
i'm standing in it
with my face up.

as much as i've grown away
from that dependency,
i'm starting to realize
how much i miss it.

having someone to hold.
the plain human physics of it —
weight, warmth, a pulse
answering yours.

missing it isn't a relapse.
it's a census:
the heart counting
what it's built to carry.

independence was the lesson.
it was never supposed
to be the life.

i might actually be lonely.
very lonely.

there. named it.
in ink, where it can't
pretend to be something else.

a named thing shrinks.
an unnamed thing runs
the whole house.

lonely is a signal, not a verdict —
the heart's porch light
saying somebody's home
and the door works.

tomorrow i use the door.
tonight, the light stays on.

items.caption:
she asked me what my idea
of the perfect girlfriend would be.

and it hit me:
if what i'm looking for
is someone who appreciates
the act of being together
more than the title —

and we already sit
for hours, unofficial,
appreciating exactly that —

then what is a title
but a frame
around a picture
that already hangs?

i left the question open.
some questions
are better as windows.

today left a lingering taste
in my mind —
an uneasy thought.

not wrong. not right.
just circling,
the way a comet circles:
gone for months,
then suddenly
all across the sky.

i'm not chasing it down.
uneasy thoughts hate patience.

i'll set out a chair
and let it land
when it's ready to talk.

i'm stirring up something
in my subconscious.
i'm stressed and confused.

good.

stirred water is cloudy
because the bottom
finally got invited
to the conversation.

everything that settles
was once in motion.
everything that shines
got dredged up first.

so stir. breathe. sleep.
by morning the water
starts sorting itself —
and whatever surfaces,
i'll be here holding the net.

items.caption:
minds are to brains
as programs are to computers.

i wrote it for the final,
but look at it —

somewhere between
the meat and the math,
a self boots up every morning
and calls itself i.

nobody knows where
the software ends
and the sky begins.

i'm a program that knows
it's running.

today that feels less like
a problem on an exam
and more like
the best news in the universe.

i saw a character
and chased him around a mall.

dream logic: escalators
that go everywhere,
storefronts selling weather,
and me, running
after some version of someone
i needed a word with.

i never caught him.
that's fine.
the chase was the message:

whatever you're after
keeps moving
because you're supposed
to keep moving.

see you tomorrow, character.
stretch first.

the day is ours.

the battle, the pages,
the dreaming, creating, learning —
as much our lives
as breathing.

two weeks of new pages now,
stacked on thirty days
of old light.

the notebook doesn't end.
it just keeps changing hands
between the me of tonight
and the me of tomorrow morning.

both of them write.
both of them read.

the day is ours.
take yours.
items.pinnedComment: new pages, same notebook. thank you for walking the way back with me. more soon. ◉
